landmarks.name: Petronas Twin Towers
landmarks.writeup: Iconic twin skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, once the tallest buildings in the world, symbolizing Malaysia's modernization.

landmarks.name: Batu Caves
landmarks.writeup: A limestone hill with a series of caves and cave temples, famous for the large statue of Lord Murugan and Hindu festivals.

landmarks.name: George Town
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its colonial architecture, street art, and multicultural heritage.

landmarks.name: Mount Kinabalu
landmarks.writeup: The highest peak in Southeast Asia, located in Sabah, popular for trekking and biodiversity.

landmarks.name: Langkawi Islands
landmarks.writeup: An archipelago known for its beaches, rainforests, and duty-free shopping.

head_of_state: Yang di-Pertuan Agong Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah

cultural_events.name: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
cultural_events.writeup: A major Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with feasts and family gatherings.

cultural_events.name: Chinese New Year
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated by the Chinese community with lion dances, fireworks, and family reunions.

cultural_events.name: Deepavali
cultural_events.writeup: The Hindu festival of lights, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness.

cultural_events.name: Thaipusam
cultural_events.writeup: A Hindu festival involving a pilgrimage and acts of devotion, notably at Batu Caves.

cultural_events.name: Malaysia Day
cultural_events.writeup: Commemorates the formation of Malaysia on September 16, 1963.

food_writeup: Malaysian cuisine is a vibrant blend of Malay, Chinese, Indian, and indigenous influences, featuring dishes like nasi lemak, laksa, satay, and roti canai, known for its rich spices and diverse flavors.
brief_history: Malaysia was historically a center of trade and colonial interest, ruled by the British until gaining independence in 1957. It formed Malaysia in 1963 by uniting Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore (which left in 1965). The country has since developed into a multi-ethnic, rapidly industrializing nation.

important_people.name: Tunku Abdul Rahman
important_people.description: First Prime Minister and founding father of Malaysia

important_people.name: Mahathir Mohamad
important_people.description: Long-serving Prime Minister known for modernization policies

important_people.name: Sultan Abdul Samad
important_people.description: Historical ruler during British colonial period

current_conflicts: Malaysia is generally stable but faces occasional tensions related to ethnic relations, territorial disputes in the South China Sea, and issues with illegal immigration and border security.
